results.content:
# Hevy Alternatives: 6 Workout Trackers Worth Switching To

Quick answer: The best Hevy alternatives depend on why you are leaving. Choose FitNotes for a genuinely free offline logger, Strong for the fastest tap-to-log interface, Boostcamp for ready-made programs, a plain notes app for total flexibility, a spreadsheet for full control, and Gym Note Plus if you want to log in plain text and still get automatic charts.

Hevy is a good app. That is worth saying up front, because most "alternatives" articles pretend the incumbent is terrible.

People usually leave it for one of three reasons: they hit a free-tier limit, they find the set-by-set tapping slower than just typing, or they never wanted a social feed in the first place.

. . .

## Why do people look for a Hevy alternative? [...] > The best workout tracker is not the one with the most features. It is the one you still open on the fourth set of a bad Tuesday.

## Frequently Asked Questions

### What is the best free alternative to Hevy?

FitNotes is the best fully free alternative to Hevy for Android users, since it has no premium tier and no ads, offering offline logging and progress graphs at no cost. On iOS, a plain notes app is the most common free option, though it provides no charts or automatic analysis. Gym Note Plus offers plain-text logging with automatic charts.

### Is Strong better than Hevy? [...] Be honest about which one is yours. Switching apps for the wrong reason means you switch again in three months.

## What is the best free Hevy alternative?

### FitNotes

FitNotes is the strongest choice if "free" is the requirement and you are on Android. It has no premium tier and no ads, which is genuinely rare.

It is a fast offline logger with clean progress graphs and no video demos, no AI suggestions, and no social feed. That minimalism is either exactly what you want or exactly what you will miss.

 Best for: Android lifters who want a free, permanent, offline log.
 Watch out for: No iOS version, and the interface looks its age.

results.content:
1. What is the best Hevy alternative?

Well, the best alternative depends on what you're missing. For hands-off algorithmic programming, Fitbod scored highest in our testing (7.8/10). For free, proven, coach-written programs, Boostcamp is the best pick. If you want training and nutrition together, TheBean.ai is the only option here that does both from shared data.

2. Is there a free Hevy alternative that's actually good?

Simply, it’s Boostcamp. Its free tier is the real app, not a trial: 11,000+ programs, full tracking, RPE logging, and analytics with no time limit. It's the rare "free" app that doesn't lock the good stuff behind a paywall.
